She’s proving that, once again, she has a full Christmas dance card as she’s continuing to bring in the holiday cheer with products available through her KHY brand. The holiday wear features a black, white, pink, and olive color scheme for a more Kardashian/Jenner-esque aesthetic.

See if you can spot some SKIMS fits or fun holiday looks in Season 8 of The Kardashians, which hit the 2026 TV schedule in early October and will continue into December. New episodes can be watched every Thursday with a Hulu subscription.

(Christine shares six kids with her ex-husband. She has since moved on with David Woolley, whom she wed in October 2023.)

Janelle, meanwhile, was spiritually married to Kody from 1993 to 2022 before the end of their relationship.

Meri, for her part, was legally married to Kody from 1990 to 2014. She agreed to legally divorce the Wyoming native at the time so he could legally wed Robyn, 48, and adopt her three children from a prior marriage.

Meri and Kody, who share one child, remained in a spiritual relationship for almost another decade before she confirmed in January 2023 that they were no longer married.

Robyn, who shares two biological children with the patriarch, is still legally married to Kody.

#3594. Ken Paxton: The Best Photos From the Texas Republican Senate Candidate’s “Come and Take It Tour”

Down in Texas, there’s an extraordinary Senate race unfolding between a deeply flawed candidate and a very surprising Democrat. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton overcame long-tenured incumbent John Cornyn in the Republican primary thanks to President Donald Trump’s endorsement, despite a long history of scandal. That background and Trump’s remarkable unpopularity have helped put the state within reach for James Talarico, a Democratic state lawmaker and pastor who maintains a steady but narrow lead in the polling. #3592. Daniel Craig's Taut 92-minute Thriller Is Blowing Up on Streaming

The 007 star's lesser-known thriller is climbing the HBO Max charts

Daniel Craig has established himself as one of Hollywood's most reliable leading men, particularly when it comes to action movies and suspenseful thrillers. From his gritty breakout role in Layer Cake to the high-stakes mysteries of Knives Out and The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo, Craig has built an impressive filmography outside his best-known role as James Bond.

Craig played the iconic British spy across five films, beginning with Casino Royale in 2006 and concluding with No Time to Die in 2021. Now, with the search for his successor officially underway, movie fans have another reason to revisit the franchise and Craig's career as a whole.

But while audiences wait to find out who will inherit Bond's license to kill, one of Craig's more overlooked thrillers is attracting attention on streaming. The film wasn't exactly a hit with critics when it first arrived, but that hasn't stopped viewers from giving it another look.

Dream House, a 2011 psychological thriller directed by Jim Sheridan, is currently climbing HBO Max's international movie charts, according to FlixPatrol. It's ranked #3 in several countries.

Dream House follows Will Atenton (Daniel Craig), a successful publisher who leaves his job in New York City to move his wife, Libby (Rachel Weisz), and their two daughters to a quiet New England town.

Their fresh start takes a disturbing turn when Will discovers that their new home was previously the scene of a gruesome murder. A mother and her two children were killed inside the house, and the surviving husband was suspected of committing the crime. With the help of Ann Patterson (Naomi Watts), a neighbor who was close to the murdered family, Will begins investigating the tragedy. However, the deeper he digs, the more unsettling the mystery surrounding the house becomes.

Unfortunately, Dream House wasn't particularly well received when it premiered in 2011. The film currently holds a dismal 7% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes, alongside a somewhat more forgiving 36% audience score. Critics largely took issue with its slow pacing and predictable psychological thriller twists.

That's hardly the kind of reception that inspires confidence in a thriller, but more than a decade after its theatrical debut, Dream House is getting another chance to find an audience.

I have an annual tradition of watching the best horror movies, and given that Backrooms was so buzzed about earlier this year, I streamed it with my HBO Max subscription. I'd heard some people who saw it found it boring, and while I disagree on that front, I do think it isn't really scary.

The concept of "the backrooms" has existed on the internet for a long time, and I've seen it portrayed across many short films, video games, and horror stories. I wouldn't say I went into this movie with high expectations, but I certainly went in feeling like I'd leave feeling more scared than I was.

The problem, I think, is that I went into Backrooms expecting it to be a horror movie. As mentioned, people generally tackle this premise with a horror bent, typically with weird, deformed monsters and jump scares. This movie has zero jump scares, which bucks the trend of many modern horror movies, but I think it did it no favors.

All this to say, Backrooms is a fascinating thriller, and I really enjoyed the movie. Once I set aside the fact that I expected it to frighten me, I genuinely enjoyed the film and look forward to any future installments. In that way, it reminds me of The Silence Of The Lambs, which is another movie I'd associate with Halloween that isn't really that scary.

A sequel to Backrooms could, and certainly should, be much scarier. Now that the mainstream gets the general idea of how it all works, this is the time for director Kane Parsons to really flesh out how horrifying that concept is and what oddities can come from this space.

I've Been Looking Into Backrooms Theories, And Whoa, There's A Lot More To Unpack Than I Realized

As I mentioned before, we've already seen a lot of other works do this. A lot of what Parsons would need to add to a sequel is sitting there on the internet, and he has the power to make the mythology around it even scarier. It's what made it disappointing that the movie itself was more about being surreal rather than scary.

Without jump scares, Backrooms had me wondering how many people younger than me are genuinely terrified of a generic office layout from the 1990s. Or furniture that's clipped into walls and doors? We saw that all the time in video games growing up! That's not scary to me, that's bad graphics!

The good news is the movie did well and crushed it on streaming, so I think we're going to see the concept further evolve in the coming years. I'm fully on board with showing up for a sequel, but if this next one isn't scary, I don't think I'll stick around for the ride.

Full House might not be hailed as one of the best sitcoms of all time by many, but I have always been a massive fan of the show. I used to watch it every night on Nick at Nite and even own the entire series on DVD. I’ve always adored the Tanners and their extended family and can’t imagine any of them being played by any other actors; but it turns out that Lori Loughlin almost didn’t get to play Aunt Becky.

A majority of the Full House cast reunited at ‘90s Con in Connecticut and appeared on a panel discussing the show. During the panel, John Stamos shared his experience with the show’s creator, Jeff Franklin, when it came to casting Aunt Becky, aka his eventual long-term love interest on the show.

Lori came on at first, and I was like — I think we did some readings together before. I told [series creator] Jeff [Franklin], ‘I don’t know. She’s cute, and she’s adorable. I don’t think she’s tough enough to put Jesse in his place.’

Good casting can make or break a project, especially when it comes to the chemistry between two actors who are playing characters that are romantically linked. At the time, Full House wasn’t considered a hit by any means, so it makes sense that Stamos would want to get the casting right to ensure the show would continue.

While Stamos’ Uncle Jesse and Lori Loughlin’s Aunt Becky eventually became the best couple on the show, their relationship wasn’t always a walk in the park. Jesse was instantly smitten with Becky, as he was with most women on the show, but the same was not true for her character. Thus, it was important that Loughlin be able to play off Stamos’s character in order to build up that will-they, won’t-they tension.

Thankfully, the show’s creator didn’t listen to Stamos and did go on to cast Loughlin in the role. In turn, the When Calls the Heart actress proved Stamos wrong and put him and his character in his place on the first day of set.

Scene one, she came and she put me in my place fast. She had the perfect combination of this adorable, sweet girl. But, when it was time for me to get in trouble, you had no problem [playing] that out.

For those who don’t remember, Jesse meets Becky at the Tanner house and instantly tries to hit on her. Unlike most of the women who swoon at his feet, Becky challenged Jesse’s flirting attempts and even compared him to her baby brother, which gutted him. However, despite Becky’s apprehensions, she did end up falling for Jesse’s charm, and the two got together (for the first time) during the second season’s Christmas episode.

Hiring Loughlin turned out to be one of the best decisions, and the show steadily started to grow its fan base. It’s wild to think that she was initially only hired for six episodes and went on to become a fan favorite character. It turns out Aunt Becky was the missing piece all along.

#3587. Is This the Last Dance for Spain’s Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez?

On September 23, Maricarmen Abascal, a partially disabled 87-year-old woman, was evicted from the apartment she rented in Madrid, where she had lived her entire life. Suffering from exhaustion caused by the long struggle to keep her home and then her subsequent eviction, she was admitted to a hospital. That same day, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez addressed the United Nations General Assembly in New York, an international forum where he has often promoted his foreign policy agenda, beginning with his first visit in 2018, when the politician who had been given the nickname Mr. Handsome met many of his counterparts around the globe. While Abascal would never return to her home (she died on October 7), and her eviction sparked widespread public outrage, Sánchez spoke of reforming international organizations, criticized the United States and Israel, and called for reining in the “tech oligarchs” at the helm of social media platforms and artificial intelligence companies: “The future of our sons and daughters must take precedence over the financial interests of these techno-oligarchs.”

No one in Spain paid attention to the speech: Abascal’s eviction sparked social unrest in a country that boasts of being the fastest-growing in Europe in terms of GDP, a fact on which the Banco de España and the International Monetary Fund agree. This has positioned the country as one of the leading economies in the eurozone, with unemployment having fallen to historic lows, according to official figures. In macroeconomic terms, the country has consistently appealed to international investors during Sánchez’s eight years in office, with foreign investment having grown 34% since 2018, according to calculations by the Ministry of Economy. It’s possible that the Spanish economy is experiencing its best period of growth since the country’s return to democracy in the mid-1970s. However, inflation, housing affordability, and low wages—the minimum wage has risen from 735 euros to 1,221 euros, but has failed to boost salaries broadly—are taking a toll on this economic boom.

And, among voters, there’s a sense of mismanagement during this legislative term. There was the migration crisis in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the North African coast that saw the sudden arrival of more than 72,000 migrants in late July. (Ceuta has just over 83,000 residents.) The crisis was not enough to get Sánchez to cut short his vacation. It revealed clashes between the ministers of defense and the interior, and it has taken nearly three months for the situation to be brought fully under control. Political scientist and university professor Lluís Orriols noted in El Periódico that the government had come out “badly” in its handling of crises such as the one in Ceuta and the eviction of Abascal—problems compounded by “legislative paralysis” (the government has managed to pass fewer than 40 laws in this legislative session, down from more than 100 in the previous one) and “corruption.” He asserted that only the strength of the economy had prevented “a government in shambles.”

After elections in 2023, Sánchez managed to secure another term, but without a clear left-wing majority, he had to rely on the support of several right or center-right nationalist parties without a legislative pact, which led to numerous parliamentary defeats. The coalition has failed to provide Spain with an effective government. The international landscape has not been particularly favorable either. Sánchez has gradually lost his key allies: That group of young, charismatic left-wing leaders who seemed to set the global agenda and had a special rapport with the Spanish leader have long since left power—the photos showing the admiration for Sánchez from Sanna Marin of Finland, Justin Trudeau of Canada, and Jacinda Ardern of New Zealand are now a thing of the past. His rapport with other European leaders such as Emmanuel Macron, a relationship marked by effusive camaraderie since way back in 2018, is of little use now that France is in turmoil and advocates for a return to austerity are gaining power in Europe. Even his relationship with Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission and one of Sánchez’s main supporters in the European Union, despite their ideological differences, is now of little relevance.

To top it all off, the prime minister came under fire even at Harvard, where he went shortly after his speech at the General Assembly to discuss AI, only to face sharp questions about Spanish politics and corruption. Even his safe role as a statesman was being eroded by political reality. Upon returning from his trip, an attempt to pass legislation that would prevent future situations like Abascal’s (in 2025 alone, there were more than 25,000 evictions, according to data from the General Council of the Judiciary) ran into obstacles in Spain’s fragmented parliament, which rejected every measure, and the legislative session came to a close. Meanwhile, the streets of Madrid and other cities began to fill with tents as people camped out in protest in a country where housing prices are rising by more than 10% annually, well above inflation and more so than wages. Whether it’s a matter of buying (nearly three out of every four Spaniards live in an owner-occupied home) or renting, both the Ministry of Housing and the real estate portal Idealista (which typically lists nearly half a million homes) reported price increases ranging from 30%–40% nationwide, going up to 70% in high-demand areas, during the eight-year period of progressive government, exceeding even the real estate bubble that triggered a 2008 crisis coinciding with the global financial crisis. The country is only just beginning to recover from its impact.

The half-hearted measures approved in previous years to tackle the problem ran into resistance from Spain’s regional governments and city councils controlled by the opposition—the center-right Partido Popular (PP), which governs 13 of Spain’s 19 regions. “Exactly,” the mayor of Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, said on X in 2021, when opponents accused him of doing “nothing” to tackle the rental crisis in the capital, where the average rent already exceeds the minimum wage.

On October 5, following a tumultuous legislative session in a divided Congress (the more powerful of the two houses in Spain’s parliament), Sánchez announced a snap election. Two days later, Maricarmen Abascal died in the hospital.

If Sánchez loses this election—and even the most optimistic nongovernmental polls, just over a month before the election, give him only between a 5% and 10% chance of winning another term—one of the world’s last bastions of social democracy will disappear along with him. Perhaps the most significant one, both because of the influence Spain has gained within the EU in recent decades and because of the personal leadership Sánchez has exercised in global geopolitics, with the prime minister having spoken out on issues such as climate change; digital governance of AI; the war in Gaza; and, in recent days, European support for Ukraine and migration management. This last issue has even pitted him against another of Europe’s last remaining social democrats (who is also in a precarious coalition), Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen. “Sánchez is the last social democrat who defends a migration policy that is compatible with human rights,” explains political scientist Pablo Simón, a university professor and specialist in electoral systems and political parties, “and he is committed to feminism and environmentalism. Once he leaves office, Spain will be more in line with the majority of Europe and its governments.”

Policies that Sánchez has implemented domestically include granting ministerial status to the 2030 Agenda, elevating the energy transition and the fight against climate change to the level of vice presidency during his terms, and creating the first agencies in any EU country dedicated to AI governance. He has also boasted about these achievements in flawless English—still a novelty among Spanish prime ministers, who have not been particularly fond of languages—at numerous international events. All of this has taken place at a time when the established world order is collapsing, and he has emerged as one of the world leaders who most vocally opposes Donald Trump. When he denied Trump the use of Spanish bases to attack Iran, he directly accused the American president of using “the smoke of war to hide his failure and, in the process, line the pockets of a select few.”

But support for Gaza (not only does Spain recognize Palestine as a state, but Sánchez has also strongly denounced Israel’s actions and labeled them as genocide) and opposition to warmongering leaders like Trump do not win elections on their own. “The debates in Spain are quite similar to those across Europe and focus on the cost of living and immigration, which explain the discontent with governments in many countries,” Simón explains, painting a picture that affects social democrats like Sánchez, leaders further to his right like Macron, and even hard-liners like Giorgia Meloni. The problems of inflation, low wages, loss of purchasing power, and strains on the welfare state are taking their toll on nearly every government in Europe.

Sánchez is, in fact, something of an anomaly with his eight years of resistance—he even titled his book about his political life Manual de Resistencia (Manual of Resistance). Looking ahead to these elections, it appears, on paper, almost impossible for Sánchez to retain his leadership. But if anything has defined his political career, it’s his ability to survive at the last moment, aided by the sociological realities of Spain. Ignacio Urquizu, director of Metroscopia and an election expert, explained a few days ago on SER, Spain’s leading radio network, that it “is the most left-leaning country in Europe, surpassed only by Malta.” He also noted that, since the 1980s, “there has been a straight line” showing that 45% of Spanish society consistently identifies as left-wing or center-left.

Sánchez has always relied on that reality for his historic comebacks. He went from being forced to resign in 2016 as secretary-general of the PSOE (the Spanish socialist party), under pressure from the party apparatus, to regaining that position just two years later and becoming prime minister on the back of a no-confidence motion against corruption, the first of its kind to succeed in Spain. The then future prime minister denounced the corruption that caused “embarrassment, disbelief, and outrage.” He has since survived two elections with the odds stacked against him, without clear majorities, in a Spain that is no longer defined by parties but by blocs, where different forces compete for similar political spaces, leading to parliaments that the framers of Spain’s constitution never anticipated.

The most dramatic of these occurred in 2023, when the right was already uncorking the Champagne, and a single member of parliament tipped the balance in favor of the socialist coalition. It was a poisoned chalice, as Spain has seen: The fact that the PP leader did not become prime minister, due to his failure to reach agreements with several nationalist right parties, paved the way for an ineffective legislative session, with 11 parties and a minority government entangled in parliamentary gridlock and social measures often being blocked by the “no” votes of Sánchez’s supposed allies. This miracle of resilience, in any case, has somehow lasted until now. Even so, Narciso Michavila, president of the social-research firm GAD3, is not ready to declare victory for the right just yet, despite what the polls say: Sánchez, he stated recently, “still has appeal,” and Michavila thinks it is still possible that he will ultimately secure another term.

But there is no denying that in the last decade in Spain, electoral politics have changed. Some of his loyal supporters during the period between 2016 and 2018 are now in prison or awaiting trial for the very corruption that Sánchez denounced. Former minister José Luis Ábalos, once his greatest supporter and whom he even mentioned in the no-confidence-motion speech that eventually led to his becoming prime minister, has now been given a 24-year prison sentence for corruption. Santos Cerdán, the man tasked with reining in the Socialist Party, is awaiting his turn in the dock. The party leadership that came to tackle corruption has proven to be just as, if not more, vulnerable to the recurring cancer of Spanish politics as those they replaced. And although Sánchez boasted about how quickly these incidents were dealt with (there are ministers from the previous administration who are still under investigation for corruption), he has long been unable to boast of integrity as he once did, now that scandals have involved his close associates.

Meanwhile, alongside these proceedings, Sánchez, his party, and many of his allies are denouncing the “judicial persecution” that has extended to the prime minister’s family—his wife, Begoña Gómez, is awaiting trial on various corruption charges, which the prosecutor’s office has opposed on the grounds of insufficient evidence (she has denied the allegations); his brother, David Sánchez, is appealing a nine-year disqualification from holding public office imposed on him by a court in Badajoz for administrative misconduct, stemming from his holding a public position as a cultural manager that was allegedly created specifically for him (he has denied the allegations). Pedro Sánchez has claimed that his brother and wife are “innocent” and victims of a “harassment and bullying operation.”

The latest chapter in this series of trials and investigations surrounding Sánchez was particularly painful for his party and his base: Former Socialist Party president and prime minister of Spain from 2004 to 2011 José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero (who was very active in the last election campaign and served as a role model for Sánchez and his vision of progressivism) was indicted in spring 2026 over an alleged corruption scheme. Jewelry valued at more than a million euros, which Zapatero took months to clarify was supposedly a gift from the Saudi monarchy, was discovered during the searches and sealed his fate. (He has denied any wrongdoing.) The role model Sánchez had looked up to and who boasted of having led the least corrupt government in the history of Spain’s democracy suddenly became the first former prime minister in the country’s democratic history to testify as a defendant. The case is still in the preliminary investigation phase.

But at first, the PSOE came out in force, through press releases and statements from its leaders, to denounce the alleged act of lawfare with the phrase “Whoever can act, should act.” It was a direct quote from the former president of the Partido Popular, José María Aznar, when he attempted to rally opposition to Sánchez’s alliance with Catalan parties in 2023.

These tensions within his family and his party, and the blurring of the lines between the two that the opposition accuses him of, have also spilled over into his campaign. This has put his wife and the developments in her legal case in the spotlight. Sánchez declared he was “deeply in love with” Gómez when he threatened to resign in 2024, following the media harassment of her. “They’ve tried to break us in every way possible, and they’ve achieved exactly the opposite; today we’re more united and stronger than ever,” the prime minister told his wife. “Let them hear it loud and clear: I love you.” The prime minister and his wife’s campaign kisses date back to at least 2016, but this time the Socialist Party has taken up the cause: “We are the party of love,” declared Minister Óscar Puente, and the prime minister has even worn a T-shirt bearing the campaign slogan “La Fuerza del Amor” (“The Power of Love”).

Meanwhile, the far right is poised to become the country’s third-largest political force, now that measures to contain it have failed in Spain, as they have elsewhere in Europe. No measures have succeeded in curbing its rise—or, in cases like Italy, its success at claiming direct power. Spain has, however, long been a country that leans more to the left; it is perhaps the most socially left-leaning country in all of Europe.

“The truth is that the Iberian Peninsula as a whole leans a bit further to the left than its neighbors due to its historical legacy,” says Simón. “In fact, because of this history, socialist parties fare better in Spain and Portugal, and they also do well in the Scandinavian countries.” On the other hand, one need only look at France, where the once all-powerful Socialist Party is now politically irrelevant, to understand the situation in much of the rest of Europe, where centrist parties have lost their influence.

It was the mobilization of Spain’s historic left-leaning majority that saved the PSOE in 2023. This had repercussions in Europe: While other social democratic leaders were falling and the centrists or moderate right-wingers were losing momentum, Sánchez became the voice of a progressive Europe. Emmanuel Macron, who, with Sánchez, built a sort of Spanish-French axis within the European Union, now watches as France burns, six months before an election in which the far right is almost guaranteed to reach at least the runoff round. And all this is unfolding in the midst of what has been described as “Russiagate,” with “foreign interference in all democratic processes in the European Union, including disinformation.”

For Europe, the consequences of this electoral process have already become apparent: The Union had to decide on a far-reaching budget, which also includes the future of Ukraine—whose president has warned that the country needs an additional 70 billion euros that Europe does not currently have. This is especially true following the revelation by Poland’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, that the EU has been left on its own in its contribution to Ukraine’s defense and rearmament: “Since January of last year, the United States has not contributed a single cent to Ukraine’s defense. We, Europe, are doing it.” But the elections in Spain are the start of a chain of electoral contests—France and Italy will follow—that push the possibility of an agreement further out of reach. European negotiations often drag on for years, and any electoral upheaval can derail those already underway. One of Sánchez’s most loyal ministers, Luis Planas, for example, will not appear on any electoral lists so he can devote all his time in office to these negotiations: “Between now and the end of the year, the future of the common agricultural policy and the fisheries policy is at stake,” which in Spain accounts for nearly 9% of GDP through both direct and indirect contributions.

The elections will be held on November 29 amid a tense atmosphere: The right is resorting to personal attacks and AI-generated deepfakes against Sánchez, his wife, and his cabinet. Left-wing forces have not found a figurehead like Jean-Luc Mélenchon of the France Insoumise (France Unbowed) party and are polling at less than 10%—a situation that would leave the PSOE without strong coalition partners even if it performs well. Sánchez’s international standing and the strength of the macroeconomy will likely have little weight in an election where the focus is on basic issues including the cost of living and specifically housing. But whatever the outcome, it will likely be the first in a series of elections that may lay bare the crisis facing liberal democracies in Europe. Now without the protection of the United States, it faces two existential crises. There’s an internal crisis, marked by the rise of the far right and its contempt for human rights, and an external crisis, with the Russian threat becoming clearer by the day and commercial and technological pressure from the United States and China, which has counted Sánchez among its most important advocates in its dealings with Europe.

This story was originally published by Vanity Fair España. It was translated by John Newton.

#3586. President Donald Trump Ranks His Cabinet in Terms of Hotness

President Donald Trump was asked to rank the most attractive members of his current administration after he mentioned men’s asses on the campaign trail multiple times.

“Who is the best-looking member of your administration?” podcast host Miranda Devine asked on the Monday, November 2, episode of the “Pod Force One” podcast before listing Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “Which one of those three? Or is it somebody else? Pete Hegseth?”

After letting out a little chuckle, Trump, 80, said that Devine, 65, was possibly going to get him in trouble with his response.

“Pete’s a good-looking guy,” he shared. “You’re going to get me in big trouble when you ask me those questions. Why do you do that? I think they’re all great looking.”

Trump continued, “I’ll tell you what, Marco’s really a great hot politician in the sense that he’s done great. JD, the same thing. They’re all doing great. Scott Bessent is central casting, right? If I was going to do a movie on the Treasury, I’d pick him for the lead. They’re all good.”

The podcast episode’s release comes less than 24 hours before millions of Americans will cast their vote on Election Day.

Depending on the results in key states, the Democrats could take back control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives as Trump continues his second term as commander in chief.

In the weeks leading up to Decision Day, Trump made headlines for his comments about Ohio Sen. Jon Husted’s physique.

At an October 12 rally in Youngstown, Ohio, Trump said the former football coach and All-American defensive back at the University of Dayton had a “great ass.”

“I watched up and down,” Trump shared. “I looked at his ass, and I looked at the whole — and then I looked at his hands.”

In a separate rally on October 25, the commander in chief said, “I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true. Off the record: Women, yes, men, no, OK?” he said. “By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before, Nicki Minaj. … She’s been with us for a long time.”

Trump later expressed his belief that his comments about Husted’s butt helped him climb in the polls.

When campaigning for Rep. Mike Rogers, who is running for Senator in Michigan, Trump said, “I’d say that about your ass too, Mike, if it gets you a guaranteed victory.”

Trump’s comments about asses have grabbed the attention of late-night hosts and the ladies of The View.

As cohost Ana Navarro shared on the October 26 episode of the ABC talk show, “I can’t believe that Trump’s closing message on an election that is so close in so many places is about asses.”

There’s no shortage of outdoor security cameras, but finding one that balances video quality, battery life, and ease of use without pushing past $100 is rare. Right now, the Tapo MagCam 2K+ is on sale for $59.99 on Amazon, down from $89.99, which is its lowest price to date, according to price trackers. PCMag named it the best security camera of 2024, pointing out that while battery-powered cameras often trade convenience for frequent recharging, the MagCam 2K+ avoids that issue with a 10,000mAh battery rated to last up to 300 days per charge, depending on how often it records.

Charging happens over micro-USB, though there’s an optional Tapo A200 solar panel if you want to avoid manual recharging altogether. Video tops out at 2K resolution, with a wide 150-degree field of view that works well for driveways or side yards. During the day, footage looks sharp and detailed. At night, the camera can switch between infrared black-and-white or color video using its built-in spotlights and starlight sensor. Storage is flexible. Alerts can distinguish between people, pets, and vehicles, and those intelligent notifications are free, as highlighted by PCMag in its “outstanding” review of the MagCam 2K+. It also integrates smoothly with Alexa, Google Assistant, and IFTTT, though it doesn’t support Apple’s HomeKit. You also won’t find mechanical pan or tilt, but the fixed lens covers enough ground for most yards or porches. As for managing the camera, its companion app is intuitive, offering settings for motion sensitivity, siren activation, spotlight brightness, firmware updates, and more. Overall, the MagCam 2K+ handles the basics well and throws in a few smart features usually reserved for pricier models.

#3584. 2024's Best Action Game Is (Mostly) Just as Good in Stunning Switch 2 Port

Nintendo's newest hardware now has a great lineup of action games

Shift Up’s Stellar Blade is one of the decade’s great action games, blending together quick-paced sword combat and powerful parries. A sequel is on the way, but before it arrives, Shift Up isn’t done with the first game. It arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 later this week, the latest in a long line of satisfying Switch 2 ports, even if it shares the same issues as most of them.

Stellar Blade was originally a PlayStation 5 console exclusive when it was released in April 2024. It later came to Windows PC in June 2025, and future entries in the series might be multiplatform as well. Stellar Blade follows a soldier named Eve as she stylishly slaughters monsters called Naytibas as she tries to save humanity. She only has a singular melee weapon, her trusty sword, but, like Miyamoto Musashi in Onimusha: Way of the Sword, she can wreak havoc with it. Combos and different weapon skills are continually unlocked throughout the game, ensuring that skirmishes next feel stale. I’ve already played through the whole of Stellar Blade, but didn’t mind revisiting it on Switch 2 as Eve’s swordfighting is just that entertaining.

Eve also has several defensive options at her disposal that open up combat. Each perfect parry rattles my Switch 2 with intensity. Her blink-dodge allows her to zoom behind a foe for a devastating follow-up combo. You’ll need to master the timings on those as Stellar Blade’s enemies and bosses can pack a punch. While not quite on the level of a Soulslike in terms of its difficulty, regular enemies can still give you a hard time on Stellar Blade’s middle difficulty option.

New costumes are continuously acquired throughout, and Bayonetta-inspired outfits arrive alongside the Switch 2 edition this week. Just like the base game’s outfits, most of them are skin-tight, and don’t leave a whole lot to the imagination. The same can’t be said about some of Eve’s other outfits, which are basically lingerie. The great appeal of a Switch 2 is being able to play on the go in handheld mode on a long train ride or maybe in a park. But with how damn pervy the game is, I’m not sure if I’d want to bring it anywhere public. I’ll bide my time on flights by playing Pokémon Pokopia or Mario Kart World for the moment.

You can’t get much out of the game in handheld mode anyway. Like some other AAA releases on Switch 2, you’re looking at maybe three hours of battery life playing Stellar Blade on default settings with near-max brightness. There are a lot of things to love about the Nintendo Switch 2, but its battery life is not one of them.

Stellar Blade does look good in handheld mode, at least. Sure, the graphics won’t be quite as good as on PlayStation 5 and Windows PC, but that’s to be expected at this point. The biggest issue is in characters’ hair, something the Switch 2 struggles with repeatedly. Eve has an outlandishly long ponytail, which barely renders during gameplay. In cutscenes, all characters’ hair is crunchy, like their hairstyles exist in 240p. Everything else — enemy models, environments, cutscenes — look great in handheld.

Put your Switch 2 in docked mode, and that goes away, for the most part. Hair looks better, and overall the graphics are much more comparable to the PS5 and PC versions. Environmental aspects like bushes and rubble will still pop in off in the distance and faraway enemies will jankily stutter around, but those are minor complaints. Stellar Blade looks great during effects-heavy combat, and it runs smooth as well. I haven’t encountered any notable framerate drops, even during an intense boss fight.

All told, Stellar Blade Complete Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 is a great way to experience Shift Up’s action game ahead of the series’ next entry. It might have some graphical blemishes on Nintendo’s comparatively underpowered hardware, but those blemishes don’t quite matter during the moment-to-moment, adrenaline-pumping gameplay that Stellar Blade delivers in spades.

Stellar Blade Complete Edition will be released on Nintendo Switch 2 on Nov. 5.

Inside the NBA fans were hit with some major news last week, as longtime co-host Ernie Johnson confirmed his plan to leave the show at the end of the professional basketball season. Right now, many are simply taking the time to pay tribute to the man affectionately known as “E.J.” However, there are those who are also questioning what lies ahead for the show in the long run without Johnson. The man himself recently expressed his hope that the show will go on, and there’s also been an update on ESPN’s alleged feelings about that.

To put it mildly, Johnson is one of the mainstays of Inside, given he’s been hosting the show for 37 years now. 70-year-old Johnson announced his intention to exit the show nearly a week ago in a social media video that’s since gone viral. The veteran sports journalist confirmed that he wasn’t retiring from broadcasting entirely, though. He’ll continue to serve as a March Madness analyst and produce content under his 32 Bowties production company. Nevertheless, he’s stepping down from Inside as a way to “slow down a bit.”

Johnson recently caught up with Front Office Sports Tonight to discuss his big decision and plans for the future. When addressing what may lie ahead for his long-running basketball talk show, Johnson expressed optimism:

I don’t want to be blamed for ending Inside the NBA. I’m stepping away from my role on there. I would hope that they could continue the show in some form. And there are plenty of great studio hosts out there who could do what I do.

On paper, it would definitely make sense to keep the TNT-turned-ESPN sports show on the air, considering its popularity. It’s still hard not to wonder, however, how viewership may be affected by Ernie Johnson’s absence next season. Plus, there’s the fact that Charles Barkley has been discussing retirement again as well. With that, sources are now saying that ESPN has been giving the future some thought amid these developments.

Shaq Explains Why Inside The NBA Works, But I’m Just Loving The Ernie Johnson Detail He Revealed

Weeks before Johnson confirmed his intention to leave Inside, Barkley already indicated that his longtime co-star would do just that. The “Round Mound of Rebound” also said at the time that he was planning to exit the show after this current season as well due to him and Johnson being a “package deal.” Considering that Johnson and Barkley have shared the screen for over 25 years, their dual exits would mark a major shift. However, per FOS’ sources, ESPN remains committed to keeping the show going even without the pair.

That would theoretically leave co-hosts Kenny Smith and Shaquille O’Neal alongside two others. Interestingly, since Johnson shared his news, Barkley hasn’t said anything more about whether he’ll ride off into the sunset as well. Johnson was also asked about Barkley’s plans when he appeared on FOS Tonight, and he had this to say about him:

As for what Chuck is going to do, I have learned many many moons ago, you never try to predict what the Chuckster is going to do. But he and I have had a lot of conversations in the past about what we’re going to do, so I will leave that final word to him.

If any other Inside the NBA fans are like me, they’ll be waiting with bated breath for Charles Barkley to deliver a definitive decision. The fact that Ernie Johnson is leaving (for some well-deserved time with his loved ones) is already tough to think about, so Barkley’s exit would also be a lot. At the very least, though, it’s encouraging that ESPN is reportedly still aiming to keep the show on the air for the foreseeable future.

Check out Inside the NBA’s next broadcast, which will hit ESPN on Wednesday, November 4, with NBA Tip Off starting at 6 p.m. ET amid the 2026 TV schedule.

#3582. The 25 Best Movies on Netflix to Watch in November 2026

It can be hard to find the best movies on Netflix. We all understand the struggle of scrolling time—hours lost to wading through all of the Netflix movie options that could instead have been spent, you know, watching something. Or maybe something has been sitting patiently in your queue, waiting for someone to give you a nudge to finally press play. So, like a beacon in the night, here’s a guide to 25 of the best films within Netflix’s huge selection—including everything from landmark films to cult classics to Netflix-original hidden gems—updated monthly as films appear on and leave the platform. Take that, decision fatigue. (And if you want a list of the best shows on Netflix, we’ve got one of those too.)

Director: Colin HigginsGenre: ComedyNotable cast: Jane Fonda, Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton, Dabney Coleman, and Elizabeth WilsonMPA rating: PGRotten Tomatoes: 71%Metacritic: 58

After the passing of Dolly Parton this year, rewatching her in her first film role here can feel bittersweet, but it also proves how she was able to conquer all art forms she tried with seeming ease.

The multihyphenate icon once joked to Vanity Fair about taking the role of Doralee Rhodes, saying, “I thought, Well, if it’s a big success, I can just join in there with Lily [Tomlin] and Jane [Fonda]. And if it’s a big flop, I’ll just blame it on them ’cause nobody thinks about me being a movie star.” Parton would also get her first Oscar nomination and two Grammys for the title track, but the comedy gold of this trio taking on their sexist, egotistical, lying, hypocritical bigot boss remains a classic.

Director: James GrayGenre: Space DramaNotable cast: Brad Pitt, Tommy Lee Jones, Ruth Negga, Liv Tyler, Donald Sutherland, John Ortiz, and Natasha LyonneMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 83%Metacritic: 80

As director James Gray prepares to storm the awards season with Paper Tiger—a return to the crime genre that put him on the map—it’s maybe time to reassess his misunderstood and mishandled space elegy Ad Astra. It’s not your typical space exploration adventure, but something much more personal. Starring Brad Pitt as an astronaut who ventures to the depths of our solar system to recover his father (Tommy Lee Jones) after a failed mission, Ad Astra is a more soulful and introspective space film than most audiences were expecting. It didn’t help that post Disney merger, Fox whimpered the film into theatres. “But what has long distinguished Gray, and what rings true in even this [film], his grandest and in some ways most complex movie, is that his movies peer inward, not outward—toward longing, frustration, uncertainty, and rattled expectations, rather than toward resolution,” praised Vanity Fair about what makes Gray’s film so special.

Director: Ridley ScottGenre: HorrorNotable cast: Sigourney Weaver, Tom Skerritt, John Hurt, Ian Holm, Veronica Cartwright, Yaphet Kotto, and Harry Dean StantonMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 89

As the franchise spins its ever divisive sequels and now television shows, it all goes back to the sheer paralyzing terror of Ridley Scott’s original Alien. It’s maybe Jaws’ only rival for the title of greatest monster movie of all time, following the spaceship Nostromo as its crew is besieged by a vicious space creature that picks each member off one by one–eventually meeting its match in Sigourney Weaver’s beloved Ellen Ripley. The film’s influential, Giger-inspired aesthetic arguably remains Scott’s biggest visual calling card and one of the high-water marks for his career, which the Academy will finally recognize this year when he receives his honorary Oscar.

Director: Mati DiopGenre: DramaNotable cast: Mame Bineta Sane, Amadou Mbow, and Ibrahima TraoréMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 96%Metacritic: 85

Achingly romantic and fiercely original, Atlantics is a shape-shifting ghost story of sorts that defies simple categorization. Mati Diop’s first feature follows a young woman set to marry a man she does not love, while her lover flees their native Senegal by sea in search of work. Overnight, spirits begin to possess the townsfolk, seeking revenge against an exploitative corporation. Never less than captivating, the film features unforgettable visuals and an arresting blending of themes that make for one of the most daring Netflix originals—and signal Diop as one of the major breakthrough directors of the past decade.

Director: Paul FeigGenre: ComedyNotable cast: Kristen Wiig, Maya Rudolph, Melissa McCarthy, Rose Byrne, Chris O’Dowd, Ellie Kemper, Wendi McLendon-Covey, Jon Hamm, and Jill ClayburghMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 89%Metacritic: 75

Though Vanity Fair once posited that Bridesmaids was the best comedy of 2011 (amidst stiff competition like Crazy, Stupid, Love), by now we can safely call it the best and funniest comedy of that decade. Kristen Wiig plays a depressed woman whose best friend (Maya Rudolph) gets engaged, kicking off a slow-motion meltdown. Melissa McCarthy got an Oscar nomination as an abrasive but tough-loving puppy-stealer, and an underrated Rose Byrne should have been nominated alongside her as Wiig’s rival, who masks her own insecurities with judgment. Its unforgettable sequences come relentlessly–from Jon Hamm’s sexual lunacy to the notorious food poisoning sequence to a colonial woman churning butter on the wing of an airplane–and it’s only gotten funnier in recent years when we have been served too few comedies.

Director: Kirsten JohnsonGenre: DocumentaryMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 99%Metacritic: 89

Kirsten Johnson is always breaking the boundaries of what we think a documentary can be—never more so than in her deeply moving yet not-depressing tribute to her father on the eve of his death. Between candid interviews with her father, Dick, Johnson stages his death in various, surreally funny scenarios, such as a fall down the stairs or being struck by a rogue air conditioner. The director told Vanity Fair that making the film was an act of coping with her beloved parent’s dementia: “How can my father and I together confront the fact that he, who is irreplaceable, will disappear?” The effect is whimsical, profound, and restorative, making for the wildest study of love and loss in Netflix’s vast stable.

Director: Takashi YamazakiGenre: ActionNotable cast: Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Yuki Yamada, Munetaka Aoki, Hidetaka Yoshioka, and Sakura AndoMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 99%Metacritic: 81

We called its newly arriving sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero, one of the most anticipated films of the fall season, and for good reason. Godzilla Minus One was a surprise stateside box office success in 2023, resulting in a wholly deserved visual-effects Oscar (the first for a non-English-language film). The franchise has had many different takes over the years, but Takashi Yamazaki’s telling of the monster tale is the perfect pairing of large-scale bravura visuals and grounded human emotion. This revamp centers around the end of WW II, using the aftereffects of war to tell a human story of survivor’s guilt amidst all the destruction caused by the world’s most iconic movie monster.

Director: Alice RohrwacherGenre: DramaNotable cast: Adriano Tardiolo, Sergi López, and Alba RohrwacherMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 87

Director Alice Rohrwacher earned a legion of new fans from 2023’s Josh O’Conner–led La Chimera—but prior to that masterpiece, she made another with this idiosyncratic fable. Another foray into symbolic magical realism, the story of frozen-in-time sweetheart farmhand Lazzaro is used by Rohwacher to weave a magical examination of class and exploitation. Around its midpoint, the film takes a daring leap that recontextualizes everything we have seen as more than meets the eye, setting the tender Lazzaro on a course for tragedy to come. It’s one of Rohrwacher’s bespoke visual wonders that seem to commune with some kind of cinematic deity, casting a spell that lingers long after viewing.

Director: Michael MannGenre: CrimeNotable cast: [Deep breath] Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Val Kilmer, Tom Sizemore, Amy Brenneman, Natalie Portman, Ashley Judd, Dennis Haysbert, Mykelti Williamson, Jon Voight, Wes Studi, and at least a dozen moreMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 84%Metacritic: 76

Audiences were initially slightly underwhelmed by Heat in 1995—while they were promised a fireworks showdown between Al Pacino and Robert De Niro for the first time onscreen, director Michael Mann gave them something more introspective and psychological. Heat is instead something of an existential heist epic that took a few years for folks to really appreciate. Now considered Mann’s defining masterpiece, the film has earned a devoted, die-hard cult following. Thirty years on, this crime thriller is finally appreciated for being more than an action film—its sensory precision is as captivating as its brooding, masculine psychology.

Director: Azazel JacobsGenre: DramaNotable cast: Carrie Coon, Natasha Lyonne, Elizabeth Olsen, Jovan Adepo, and Jay O. SandersMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 98%Metacritic: 83

Carrie Coon, Natasha Lyonne, and Elizabeth Olsen give three revelatory performances as diametrically opposed estranged siblings—the dictator, the hippie, and the burnout, respectively. They cram together in a tiny New York City apartment as they await the death of their father. They battle over groceries, monologue about the Grateful Dead, and try (and fail) to keep their many past resentments at bay. Sure, His Three Daughters is at times a painful watch, brimming with claustrophobic tension and biting wit. But writer-director Azazel Jacobs gives this chamber piece on death and family a light touch, lifting it off into something unexpected in its emotional depth and making for one of 2024’s best films.

Director: Brett HaleyGenre: RomanceNotable cast: Blythe Danner, Sam Elliott, Martin Starr, June Squibb, Mary Kay Place, Rhea Perlman, and Malin AkermanMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 75

Featuring one of the standout performances of Blythe Danner’s career, I’ll See You in My Dreams was a bittersweet, small-scale hit in 2015. Danner stars as a widowed woman who gets a new lease on life when she tiptoes back into dating, resulting in a love affair with a dashing Sam Elliott. It’s a delicate and memorable tale of aging—not only due to Danner’s incredible performance, but also because of its surprising musical edge (Danner sings again onscreen) and delightful trio of actors as Danner’s hilarious friends: June Squibb, Mary Kay Place, and Rhea Perlman. Elliott is also a remarkable romantic star here, and this film (paired with another strong performance in Grandma the same year) helped kick off a career resurgence for the star that culminated in his first Oscar nomination in 2019 for A Star Is Born.

Director: Martin ScorseseGenre: CrimeNotable cast: Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci, Harvey Keitel, Bobby Cannavale, Ray Romano, Stephen Graham, Jesse Plemons, Jack Huston, Marin Ireland, and Anna PaquinMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 95%Metacritic: 94

Martin Scorsese’s epic fable on legacy, loyalty, and unions follows the life of Mob hit man Frank Sheeran, played by Robert De Niro. As Vanity Fair put it, “There’s something crucial about sitting with the same actors for so long. It communicates the weight and ravages of time more keenly than if the actors had been swapped out halfway through.” Much was made of the de-aging visual effects that allowed De Niro to play the character at all stages of Sheeran’s life, as was about Netflix’s refusal to play ball with the theater chains for the film’s limited theatrical release. Now that all that dust has settled, what remains is one of the defining masterpieces of this late stage of Scorsese’s career, one with a lot to say about where to place your loyalties and priorities in life.

Director: David LeanGenre: Epic dramaNotable cast: Peter O’Toole, Omar Sharif, Alec Guinness, Anthony Quinn, Jack Hawkins, Claude Rains, and José FerrerMPA rating: PGRotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 100

Netflix is not prone to offering many films from before the 1990s, so when a landmark work is on the platform, attention must be paid. David Lean’s masterpiece is widely beloved for good reason: In telling of the WW I exploits of T.E. Lawrence, Lean crafted a vivid cinematic language that would be emulated by the best directors for generations to come. Indelibly tied to the legacy of its star, Peter O’Toole, the film remains the gold standard for war epics and biopics about complicated historical figures alike. Though the film has often been trimmed and abbreviated in various releases over its lifetime, Netflix is streaming the “restored version,” which offers the film in full three-hour-and-47-minute splendor—the trick is not minding that it’s long!

Director: Rian JohnsonGenre: Sci-fiNotable cast: Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Bruce Willis, Emily Blunt, Jeff Daniels, Paul Dano, Garret Dillahunt, Noah Segan, and Piper PeraboMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 84

Rian Johnson may have spent the last decade in the realm of multiple franchises, between Benoit Blanc and Star Wars, but his first hit came with 2012’s heady sci-fi film Looper. The film casts Joseph Gordon-Levitt as a futuristic assassin tasked with killing his older self (played to career-topping brilliance by Bruce Willis) via time travel. As you might expect, nothing goes to plan. But this is just the beginning of Johnson’s unexpected twists, including an incredible performance from Emily Blunt that showed off for the first time her ability to balance action-star bravado with emotionally affecting pathos. Even after Johnson’s head-spinning, big-budget success, this is maybe the biggest benchmark for his ability to deliver something that’s several steps ahead of the audience.

Director: Todd HaynesGenre: DramaNotable cast: Natalie Portman, Julianne Moore, Charles MeltonMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 86

Todd Haynes’s darkly comedic, sleazy satire stars Natalie Portman as an actor who becomes obsessed with the real-life figure she is about to play: a former teacher (Julianne Moore) who became a tabloid fixture for her sexual relationship with a teenage student (Charles Melton). As much as the film skewers tabloid culture (it’s loosely inspired by Mary Kay Letourneau), it’s also a darkly comedic look at performance and the lies we tell ourselves. In calling it one of the best films of 2023, Vanity Fair wrote, “May December could probably be endlessly unpacked, so varied are its tones and textures and piercing insights.”

Director: Christopher NolanGenre: Noir thrillerNotable cast: Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss, Joe Pantoliano, Stephen Tobolowsky, and Harriet Sansom HarrisMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 94%Metacritic: 83

Who? Christopher Nolan? Oh yeah, heard of him! As the world-adored director takes audiences back to early civilization this summer with The Odyssey, Netflix takes you back to his early career with the neo-noir dazzler Memento. His sophomore feature, the film made major waves by telling its grimy vigilante tale from the beginning and the end, working both backward and forward until it all meets in the middle for a shocking twist. The creative editing trick put Nolan’s name on the map, propelling him from indie darling to must-have director for the studios, and the rest is history. If you haven’t caught up to the film, it’s proof that Nolan has always been a master of mixing up timelines in order to blow our minds.

Director: Barry JenkinsGenre: DramaNotable cast: Mahershala Ali, Trevante Rhodes, Naomie Harris, André Holland, Ashton Sanders, Jharrel Jerome, and Janelle MonáeMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 98%Metacritic: 99

Celebrating its 10th anniversary this year, Barry Jenkins’s landmark Black queer drama Moonlight follows the coming-of-age and queer acceptance of Chiron over three chapters of his life. Through childhood, teen years, and early adulthood, we see Chiron taken under the wing of a drug dealer (an immaculate and Oscar-winning Mahershala Ali) and face the addiction battles of his mother (Naomie Harris) and the inner demons of masculinity and homosexuality. “Jenkins has made a breathtaking film, one with political urgency and a deep, compassionate humanity,” said Vanity Fair in its review upon the film’s festival debut, “Moonlight is timely and timeless, a study in limits that casts its gaze up toward something transcendent.” While we remember the fraught circumstances of its best picture win at the Academy Awards, the film remains one of the key masterpieces of this generation of filmmakers.

Director: Paul Thomas AndersonGenre: RomanceNotable cast: Daniel Day-Lewis, Vicky Krieps, Lesley Manville, and Harriet Sansom HarrisMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 90Now that Paul Thomas Anderson has won his Oscar(s) with last year’s One Battle After Another, we can rest easy knowing that his eccentric filmography has finally been recognized. But his most atypical film is perhaps 2017’s Phantom Thread, a romance that’s swoony and caustic in equal measure. Demanding diva couturier Reynolds Woodcock (Daniel Day-Lewis, in what was then supposed to be his final performance) falls for straight-shooting waitress Alma (Vicky Krieps, in her breakout role), resulting in a marriage that by turns fuels Reynolds’s creative inspiration and has them hilariously at each other’s throats. In true PTA fashion, any tenderness is never without its sharp corners, but it’s nevertheless his most sumptuous movie.

Director: Jane CampionGenre: DramaNotable cast: Benedict Cumberbatch, Kirsten Dunst, Jesse Plemons, Kodi Smit-McPhee, Thomasin McKenzie, Keith Carradine, and Frances ConroyMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 94%Metacritic: 89

Jane Campion’s big-screen return earned high praise for its psychologically intense study of masculinity in the American West. It’s never quite the movie you expect: In calling it one of 2021’s best films, Vanity Fair critic Richard Lawson said this “stately and mysterious film isn’t quite a character-study drama, not quite a thriller, and not really a Western. It is an elusive and mesmerizing thing unto itself.” An all-consuming visual experience, The Power of the Dog features top-to-bottom outstanding performances from its cast, including Benedict Cumberbatch as one of the most terrifying movie villains in recent memory. It’s not just one of the best movies on Netflix right now; it’s one of the best movies ever.

Director: Tamara JenkinsGenre: ComedyNotable cast: Paul Giamatti, Kathryn Hahn, Molly Shannon, John Carroll Lynch, Kayli Carter, and Denis O’HareMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 94%Metacritic: 83

In one of Netflix’s best movies and most overlooked masterworks, Kathryn Hahn and Paul Giamatti star as an infertile New York City couple who, after several unsuccessful attempts at fertility treatment, consider surrogacy with their wayward niece (Kayli Carter). It’s only the third entry in writer-director Tamara Jenkins’s (flawless) filmography, but it’s maybe the best showcase of her bittersweet comic pathos yet: There’s nude ranting, people shoving their feet in their mouths, and bits about overly specific lox portions. If the film’s final shot doesn’t heal whatever ails you, please consult your doctor. All that, plus a powder keg, career-best performance from Hahn–before she would become a household name with her MCU debut as Agatha in WandaVision–makes this essential viewing.

Director: Alfred HitchcockGenre: ThrillerNotable cast: Anthony Perkins, Janet Leigh, Vera MilesMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 97%Metacritic: 97

Cue the sharp violin strings because it’s Hitchcock-tober! This notorious game-changing thriller that made an entire generation afraid to go into the shower remains Hitchcock’s most iconic movie for a reason. It practically invented the plot twist, and it has two of them that movies have been borrowing from since. However, Psycho still reigns supreme for its narrative nerve and pervy ability to shock, led by Anthony Perkins’s tetchy, slowly unnerving performance as the killer, Norman Bates. Like the aforementioned Lawrence of Arabia, Psycho is currently one of the rare films from before the 1990s available on Netflix, so for folks looking more for film history (whether for a rewatch or a first watch), now is the time.

Director: Rob ReinerGenre: Coming-of-age dramaNotable cast: Wil Wheaton, River Phoenix, Corey Feldman, Jerry O’Connell, Kiefer Sutherland, and Richard DreyfussMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 89%Metacritic: 76

After Rob Reiner’s tragic death, the love for his greatest cultural touchstones was reignited. Though he gave us such beloved films as When Harry Met Sally…, Misery, and The Princess Bride, many would still anoint Stand by Me as his career peak—not for nothing, Vanity Fair has called it the best Stephen King movie. Based on King’s novella The Body, it follows a group of young friends who go in search of a dead body in the wilderness, gently touching on themes of death and masculinity that bruise us in much the same way that the experience does its young heroes. Forty years on, it’s still an enduring classic about the trials of growing up—and for good reason.

Director: Yance FordGenre: DocumentaryMPA rating: UnratedRotten Tomatoes: 100%Metacritic: 86

Ford tackles his own family history and the injustice of the legal system with this nonfiction stunner, a recounting of his brother’s 1992 murder and how the killer went free. Where other documentaries navel-gaze at the details of a murder, Strong Island is more interested in the aftermath of the crime—how his brother’s killer going free shaped both his identity and his family’s. Ford approaches such personal subject matter with a sober and unflinching formal rigor, including some audacious moments where he directly addresses the camera. The result is a film that’s something of an antidote to the rise of the exploitative true crime documentary, a deeply intimate and searingly introspective portrait of a still-grieving family denied justice.

Director: Sarah PolleyGenre: DramaNotable cast: Michelle Williams, Seth Rogen, Luke Kirby, and Sarah SilvermanMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 79%Metacritic: 68

Sarah Polley is one of the greatest living multihyphenates (she’s acted and written books with equal brilliance!), but her directorial output has proven to be the most singular part of her career. Between giving Julie Christie a career resurgence with Away From Her and winning an Oscar for Women Talking, Polley made a more divisive film in the infidelity character study Take This Waltz. The sexy, frankly observed film stars Michelle Williams as a young woman who, despite her idyllic life, finds herself surprisingly adrift as she approaches 30, leading her to drift away from her all-too-perfect husband, played by Seth Rogen (before he would bring Polley out of acting retirement for The Studio). The movie makes some uncomfortable, perhaps because it’s unflinchingly honest (and nonjudgmental) about the displacement we can feel at a certain stage of our life.

Director: Todd FieldGenre: DramaNotable cast: Cate Blanchett, Nina Hoss, Noémie Merlant, Adam Gopnik, and Mark StrongMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 93

After a 16-year absence, director Todd Field returned with Tár, a story of ego and disgrace for a fallen conductor, played with towering conviction by (a maybe career best) Cate Blanchett. “Field’s film is enormous, contemplating the end of idolism in all its loss and revolution,” raved Vanity Fair. “Tár bracingly responds to the dawning of a new era and reintroduces the world to a filmmaker who seems only better for having taken some time, a very long time indeed, to listen and to learn.” What’s immediately apparent is the precision with which Field takes to this dissection of a post-#MeToo downfall of a powerful person who has done bad things (with the film told entirely from their myopic perspective), but a rewatch reveals it’s also ruefully funny as well.

#3581. Southern Charm’s Taylor Happy to 'Have Life Back' After 'Unfaithful' Exes

Southern Charm alum Taylor Ann Green is opening up about how her life has changed after ending two relationships with allegedly unfaithful exes.

“I couldn’t be happier to have my life back,” Taylor, 32, revealed during a Sunday, November 1, Instagram Q&A with fans.

In June, Taylor confirmed on “The Viall Files” that she’d recently split from ex-boyfriend Gaston Rojas after three years together. Taylor suspected that Gaston, 34, may have cheated on her, though she said that he denied any infidelity.

Prior to her relationship with Gaston, Taylor’s tumultuous romance with Southern Charm costar Shep Rose played out on the hit Bravo show — ultimately ending when she discovered he’d been unfaithful, too. Shep, 47, confessed that he had indeed cheated on Taylor, even saying that “sometimes it was fun” to fool around behind her back.

In light of two tough breakups back-to-back, Taylor was quite candid on Sunday when a fan asked her for “the dirty deets” about her split with Gaston.

“Really nothing to it other than finding out about an ongoing affair with a girl in New York #goknicks,” she quipped via Instagram. “The only difference between one cheating ex over the other is that one of them *cough cough* was at least man enough to admit his faults and not lie to cover it up.”

She continued, “For that, I will have (and have had) respect, forgive and move forward. We are better for it.”

Southern Charm fans have speculated that Taylor and Shep may be getting back together after they were spotted filming the Bravo reality show earlier this year. (A Southern Charm season 12 trailer showed the former couple dancing together on a cast trip to Maui, much to the dismay of Shep’s friends, Craig Conover and Austen Kroll.)

Shep remained coy about where he currently stands with Taylor while speaking to Us at Bravo Fan Fest in Charleston on October 24, cryptically hinting that “everything’s great” between them.

“We talked for 45 minutes yesterday on the phone,” he told Us.

Asked whether they might get back together, Shep slyly teased with a big grin, “You’re going to have to find out, darling.”

For her part, Taylor clarified on “The Viall Files” in June that filming Southern Charm scenes with her ex didn’t necessarily mean that they were getting back together.

“I have seen the rumors that we’re getting back together or hooking up again or whatever, and that is not true,” she stressed. “Even if I wanted to hook up with Shep again or get back together, I would hope I have a little bit more respect for myself to go from one cheating ex to the other.”

Southern Charm premieres on Bravo Thursday, November 12, at 9 p.m. ET. Stream new episodes the next day on Peacock.

#3580. Why the Holidays Are Actually the Best Time of Year to Start Working Out

If you have even the tiniest inkling that you might want to get in shape in the new year—or anytime really—don’t wait until January. This isn't a "winter arc" self-improvement pitch; it's just facts. The best time to start a gym habit is before the holiday season. Heck, in December, you’ll even have the place mostly to yourself.

Sure, technically “right now” is always the best time to start exercising, but the holiday season is special. If you wait until January, gyms will be packed. The first two weeks of the year, everybody thinks they’re at the start of an amazing new fitness habit...and by February, most of them have forgotten all about it. Don’t make life harder for yourself by starting during the big rush. Classes will fill up, you’ll have to fight people for the squat rack, and it will be hard to have any real fun. So start now.

In October and November, gyms and classes are at more or less their normal capacities. This is a good time to feel out the vibe of a new place. But it gets better: Once December rolls around, the fair-weather gymgoers will be off shopping for gifts after work and attending holiday parties on the weekends. They won’t feel like getting out of their warm beds in the morning, either. When you arrive, the squat rack will be free. You’ll have your choice of treadmills. The gym will be your oyster.

If you start now, you'll have about two months to get up to speed before the rush starts in January. And that is a perfect little time frame to set a small goal and keep it. Vow to hit the gym three times a week, and you’ll be able to get in 24 workouts before Christmas, even if you take a few days off for festivities. You can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Or run, if that's the fitness journey you're most excited about. If you start a couch-to-5k running plan now, you’ll be routinely running 30 minutes at a stretch by the time we get to January.

Yes, the holiday season can be busy and stressful, but remember that working out tends to help our brains manage stress. Mark workouts on your calendar, and keep those appointments with yourself.

Don’t worry about missing out on deals. Any gym or studio that offers a January special probably offers sales year-round anyway. And ultimately, if you get into the habit of actually using the gym, you're getting a lot more value for your money than somebody who joins in January and quickly stops showing up.

#3579. Brent Spiner Recalls The Hilarious Way He Landed Patrick Stewart's Saturday Night Live Hosting Gig

The Next Generation co-star played a key role.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Star Trek: The Next Generation's Brent Spiner revealed he had a small part to play in Patrick Stewart's famous time hosting Saturday Night Live. A story about the Data actor's attempt to get on the show is making rounds after his co-star's death, and I absolutely love it.

Spiner's story popped up in a special video from Dropping Names With Brent And Jonny, which compiled each time the hosts talked about their former co-star and friend, Stewart. This led to a hilarious story in which Spiner tried to get on SNL, only for them to inquire about Stewart instead:

My now-wife, she was a publicist on [TNG], and when she became a publicist she said, 'Is there anything you would like to do? I'll see if I can get that for you.' I said, 'Yeah, I want to host Saturday Night Live.' She said, 'Ok,' and she called them and she said, 'Well, I called them and they said we'd like to have Patrick Stewart.'

Brent Spiner may be the funniest person in Star Trek, which is evident enough from stories from co-stars and the Generations movie. That was enough to get him on Night Court, but Saturday Night Live is reserved for the leads. As such, their staff wanted Patrick Stewart, and as we know, Stewart is who they got.

As A Star Trek Fan I'm Eternally Grateful For What Patrick Stewart Did For The Franchise

Patrick Stewart only hosted SNL once in the 90s, but the night lives on in the show's history thanks to a story John Mulaney worked into his stand-up comedy. Mulaney stressed that Stewart's delivery when introducing Salt-N-Pepa was interesting because he sounded surprised by the Pepa bit of it, though people debate whether it really was that silly after watching the clip.

As for other stand-out moments of the Saturday Night Live appearance, there are a few skits that stand out. There's a skit I love that combined Star Trek: The Next Generation with The Love Boat, as well as another about him working in an erotic bakery shop. Both had me laughing out loud when I watched, so those who can seek it out certainly should.

It's yet another story about Stewart appearing on another show, which I found just after writing about Jeremy Clarkson having him on the set of Top Gear. I'll always appreciate the wild Star Trek stories about Stewart, but I've heard a good deal of them already. Learning his experience on other shows is great, and further illustrates what kind of man he was behind the scenes.

Both his Star Trek and Marvel co-stars insist that Patrick Stewart was exceptionally kind. He played a Captain on television and a super-powered Professor in the X-Men, and by all accounts, both were a good show of just how heroic he was as a real-life individual. As a fan, it's great to see the man measured up to all I imagined he'd be.

CinemaBlend continues to offer condolences to the family of Patrick Stewart, and the friends who continue to mourn him. It's been great to see all the stories hitting the internet, and how it's given fans comfort in the wake of a tremendous loss to the Star Trek world.

Mick Joest is a Content Producer for CinemaBlend with his hand in an eclectic mix of television goodness. Star Trek is his main jam, but he also regularly reports on happenings in the world of Star Trek, WWE, Doctor Who, 90 Day Fiancé, Quantum Leap, and Big Brother. He graduated from the University of Southern Indiana with a degree in Journalism and a minor in Radio and Television. He's great at hosting panels and appearing on podcasts if given the chance as well.

#3578. Heidi Klum Shocks In Severed Hand Halloween Costume

Heidi Klum has done it again. The Project Runway host exceeded all our Halloween expectations by transforming herself into a giant, severed human hand nearly two meters tall for the latest edition of her annual party, held Saturday night in New York City. The costume, which required hours of work by her makeup and prop team, left no detail to chance: hyper-realistic veins modeled after her own anatomy, wrinkles, red-painted nails, and an exxagerated version of the rings she typically wears.

“Mike [Marino, from the special effects team ProRenFX] has all of these scans of my body, so he was able to use those to create an exact replica of my hand,” Klum explained to Vogue. “We wanted everything to be as realistic as possible—the anatomy, the veins, the muscles, all the little details that make a hand look like a real hand.”

The costume’s structure used the model's legs to form two of the fingers, while her right arm provided mobility for the thumb. Only her eyes and mouth were visible amid the bloody wounds on her palm, from which—to top off the gruesomeness of it all—Heidi Klum would occasionally spit out the fake blood that a team of assistants injected into her mouth. The most macabre part was at the wrist, where a horrific gash exposed a jumble of blood, bones, and torn flesh.

Heidi Klum (L) recieves an injection of fake blood to augment her 2026 Halloween costume.

Other guests at Klum's party included Kyle MacLachlan, who arrived dressed as his character from The Flintstones; Neil Patrick Harris and his husband David Burtka, dressed as the girls from The Shining; and Heidi Klum and Flavio Briatore's daughter, Leni Klum.

Before making her grand entrance, the host had built up anticipation on social media by posting clues about this year’s costume, such as a photo of her real hand that showed her wedding ring alongside the small tattoo of husband Tom Kaulitz's name. It, too, was part of her Halloween costume. “Nothing was overlooked! I love that Mike pays attention to things that most people might not even notice at first. The details make these costumes so special. It’s not just any giant hand: It’s my giant hand!” Klum said.

Heidi Klum 2026 Halloween costume, as seen from the back.

This is the 25th annual Halloween party thrown by the former Victoria’s Secret Angel: The event began in 2000, and has only continued to expand in scope. “ “Can you believe it? Twenty-five years of Halloween, costumes, incredible transformations, and so many amazing memories,” she said.

Last night’s “amputated hand” joins Klum's collection of Halloween costumes that ranges from last year’s mythological Medusa (with a petrified Kaulitz by her side) to E.T., to Shrek’s Fiona, to a disgusting giant worm inside which she feared she might suffocate. We're already looking forward to what she comes up with for next year.
